title: Assistant conversation
purpose: Choose a provider and model, send, stream, stop, retry and recover in a conversation with an assistant, preserving the submitted route and the person's words without claiming an answer is complete before it is.
useWhen: A person writes to an assistant and reads its answers as they stream.
avoidWhen: The agent's actions themselves (approve, run, recover); use the agent-action contract alongside this one.
alternatives: Use agent-action for what the agent does, and consequential-action for a person's own destructive actions.
requiredInputs: a stream that yields text and resolves only when complete
errors classified as offline, rate limited, context full, refused or outage
the restored answer and whether it completed, after a reload
the context window used, when known
when model choice is offered: an authorized provider/model catalog, a controlled pair and selection callback, with loading/error and unavailable reasons
the captured provider/model pair on submitted, queued and restored inputs, and actual response metadata when server routing can differ
transitions: submitted, streaming or awaiting-input → stopped on Stop, keeping the partial answer
submitted or streaming → failed, keeping the message, with Retry
streaming → awaiting-input while a Confirmation or Question is open, then back
a reload during streaming → interrupted, with Retry
a message written while streaming → queued with its captured provider/model, sent when the turn ends
provider change → choosing-model; a valid model choice enables the next send
catalog loading, error or unavailable selection → block new sends and queues, preserve input and keep Stop available
picker change during a turn → next-message selection changes, recorded and queued routes remain unchanged
retry or restore → retain the submitted provider/model pair and revalidate before dispatch
applicability: Conversations with an assistant, in products and harnesses.
exceptions: Persistence, retention and the transport are the application's; the contract covers what the person sees.

The application owns provider credentials, authorized catalogs, server authorization, capability validation, billing policy and saved preferences; the selector performs no inference or connection setup.
Provider/model selection is opt-in; existing single-route composers do not need a picker.
